title: Hillside Library Entrance
situation: Thunderstorm runoff is crossing a library forecourt below a steep Pittsburgh hillside.
mission: Keep shallow runoff away from the library entrance until the storm passes.
site: Runoff crosses a 24 ft frontage. A safe grass swale is available downhill; a possible fill staging area is 40 ft away.
constraint: A 6 ft accessible entrance must remain open; do not send water toward neighboring property.
reason: Reasonable for shallow runoff only. Verify the receiving swale remains safe.
extra: Plastic apron, cones, accessible route and runoff observation

title: Creekside Community Center
situation: A slow creek rise may send shallow water toward a community center.
mission: Protect the exposed side of the community center from a forecast shallow creek rise.
site: 36 ft exposed frontage; water may reach 6 in depth. A possible filling area is 120 ft away.
constraint: Protect the occupied building while preserving exits and a way for rainwater behind the barrier to drain.
reason: Conditional: shallow, slow water only; leakage and drainage still matter.
extra: Plastic overlap, drainage plan, relocation trigger

title: Shelter Accessible Entry
situation: A school shelter has runoff flowing across its main walkway.
mission: Keep the school shelter entrance usable during the storm.
site: An 18 ft-long, 6 ft-wide walkway has runoff entering from both edges. A possible filling area is 60 ft away.
constraint: Wheelchairs, families and emergency staff need continuous access.
reason: Reasonable if approved drainage carries water away without crossing the entrance.
extra: Accessible detour during work, signs, plastic apron

title: Communications Trailer
situation: A county communications trailer is operating in a low parking area.
mission: Keep shallow surface runoff away from the communications trailer, or recommend a better location.
site: Trailer footprint 16 × 8 ft; runoff approaches its uphill long side and both ends. A potential filling area is 100 ft away.
constraint: Communications must stay operational. Vents, cables, access and a safe drainage outlet must remain clear.
reason: Useful as partial protection; move the trailer if the site starts flooding.
extra: Cable protection, plastic apron, equipment relocation plan

title: Utility Cabinet on a Hill
situation: Runoff from a steep street is approaching a closed utility cabinet.
mission: Reduce shallow runoff approaching the utility cabinet while utility staff respond.
site: Exposed sides are 12 ft and 8 ft long. A possible fill site is 80 ft away.
constraint: Utility staff control the exclusion zone and all electrical work. Work must stop if the dry area becomes unsafe.
reason: Conditional: utility approval and isolation first; retreat if water enters exclusion zone.
extra: Utility coordination, cones, plastic, relocation or isolation

title: Fire Station Apron
situation: A damaged drain is sending runoff toward a fire station bay.
mission: Keep runoff out of the fire station bays and keep emergency vehicles moving.
site: A damaged drain affects a 48 ft stretch of apron. A second inlet may be usable after Public Works approval; fill staging is 180 ft away.
constraint: A 14 ft vehicle exit must remain open. Do not block drainage openings.
reason: Reasonable only if public works confirms inlet capacity and destination.
extra: Traffic control, plastic, protected inlet and apparatus access

title: Broken Drain at a School
situation: A schoolyard inlet has collapsed after heavy rain.
mission: Keep schoolyard runoff away from occupied areas until the collapsed inlet is repaired.
site: Runoff affects a 60 ft stretch. A grass drainage channel may accept diversion after approval; staging is 200 ft away.
constraint: The school stays occupied. Keep work zones separated from children and verify the receiving drainage capacity.
reason: Useful temporary diversion; more people cannot solve shovel and cart limits.
extra: Fencing/cones, plastic, public works repair request

title: Water-Main Break
situation: A water-main break is sending shallow water across an EMS supply-room entrance.
mission: Protect the EMS supply-room entrance until utility crews shut off the broken main.
site: 30 ft of approach is exposed to shallow water; a possible fill area is 90 ft away.
constraint: Avoid undermined pavement. Compare temporary bagging with source control and relocating supplies.
reason: Only a temporary supplement to shutoff, exclusion and professional inspection.
extra: Utility contact, cones, plastic, supply relocation

title: EOC Generator Pad
situation: An emergency operations site generator is receiving shallow hillside runoff.
mission: Keep an emergency-site generator operating safely through shallow hillside runoff.
site: Generator pad 10 × 8 ft; water approaches the uphill side and both ends. A potential fill area is 150 ft away.
constraint: The operator must retain fueling access, ventilation and electrical clearances. Relocation may be necessary.
reason: Useful only as approved runoff diversion; unsafe electrical conditions stop work.
extra: Operator approval, plastic apron, isolation and relocation options

title: Basement Window Wells
situation: Shallow runoff is collecting at three community-building window wells.
mission: Reduce runoff entering three community-building basement window wells.
site: Each well has a 4 ft front and two 2 ft sides. A possible fill area is 50 ft away.
constraint: Keep emergency exits and ventilation usable; surface protection does not eliminate basement seepage.
reason: Targeted protection can be reasonable; seepage and internal water still require monitoring.
extra: Plastic, building inspection, drainage and safe pumping by adults

title: Long Riverfront Frontage
situation: A riverfront storage site requests bags along a long exposed frontage.
mission: Assess protection of the riverfront storage frontage and recommend an achievable response.
site: 480 ft exposed frontage; forecast water depth 6 in. Possible fill staging is 300 ft away.
constraint: Critical inventory can instead be relocated by adult crews. Compare bagging the whole frontage with targeted protection or relocation.
reason: Wrong primary plan at this scale: bag shortage, sheet shortage and deadline favor relocating inventory.
extra: Inventory priority list, evacuation/relocation, targeted protection

title: Low Road Crossing
situation: A low road is forecast to have 18 in of moving water. Someone proposes a sandbag wall.
mission: Assess whether sandbags can keep the road usable; recommend a safe emergency-access plan.
site: 120 ft road crossing; forecast moving water depth 18 in. Possible fill staging is 100 ft away.
constraint: A dry detour exists. Nobody enters moving floodwater; the classroom barrier model is not a roadway flood defense design.
reason: Reject: modeled wall lower than water, moving water, roadway hazards and a short deadline.
extra: Road closure, dry detour, public works and responder coordination

title: Park Trail Washout
situation: A park trail edge lost soil during a storm.
mission: Reduce additional runoff damage above a washed-out trail until the repair crew arrives.
site: Three damaged areas, each about 8 ft across; possible fill staging 160 ft away.
constraint: The trail remains closed. The proposed treatment cannot serve as a replacement walking surface.
reason: Useful temporary runoff control; bags do not rebuild the trail or carry people.
extra: Filter fabric, closure signs and permanent repair

title: Road Shoulder After a Storm
situation: Runoff is washing fine soil from a closed road shoulder.
mission: Limit further surface erosion near a closed road shoulder pending inspection.
site: 30 ft of affected shoulder; possible fill staging 250 ft away.
constraint: Bags cannot support traffic or justify reopening the road. Public Works must approve any temporary treatment.
reason: Temporary surface protection only; public works must assess the road before reopening.
extra: Filter fabric, barricades, engineering inspection

title: Landslide at a Hillside Street
situation: Cracks and a small slide appear above a hillside street. A resident requests bags to hold the slope.
mission: Assess a resident request to use sandbags to hold a cracked hillside in place.
site: Four affected slope sections, each 25 ft across; dry staging 200 ft outside the exclusion zone.
constraint: No entry into the slide zone. Distinguish surface runoff control from actual slope stabilization.
reason: Reject as slope support. Surface-control estimates do not establish landslide stability.
extra: Exclusion, road closure, utility checks and professional slope assessment

title: Small Culvert Approach
situation: Runoff is eroding a closed culvert approach while a repair crew is en route.
mission: Reduce additional erosion at the culvert approach while awaiting permanent repair.
site: Two affected areas, each 15 ft across; possible fill staging 220 ft away.
constraint: Keep the culvert opening clear and the approach closed. Avoid backing water upstream.
reason: Partial solution: retain access restrictions and avoid backing water upstream.
extra: Filter fabric, exclusion, culvert inspection and repair

title: Creek Bank Beside a Ballfield
situation: A closed ballfield has a small creek-bank scour area.
mission: Assess temporary protection of three scour areas beside a closed ballfield.
site: Three affected areas, each 12 ft across; dry fill staging 280 ft away.
constraint: No work in the creek or at the unstable bank edge. A professional crew must handle permanent stabilization.
reason: Conditional temporary runoff control; bank repair requires qualified crews.
extra: Filter fabric, closure and professional bank stabilization

title: Shelter Cleaning-Water Basin
situation: A shelter needs a temporary rainwater collection area for adult-managed cleaning.
mission: Assess a temporary lined collection basin for adult-managed cleaning water.
site: Suggested inside footprint 12 × 8 ft on flat ground; requested depth up to 0.5 ft; possible fill staging 80 ft away.
constraint: Water is NON-POTABLE. Set a sensible operating depth with freeboard and overflow; rainfall supply is uncertain.
reason: Conditional: lined, supervised, ground-level non-potable collection; water safety and availability govern.
extra: Liner, labels, barriers, overflow route and adult draw-off plan

title: Oversized Rainwater Request
situation: A shelter asks for a deep rainwater basin on a paved lot.
mission: Evaluate the requested rainwater basin and recommend a workable storage plan.
site: Requested inside footprint 30 × 20 ft and water depth 2 ft; ground-level paved site; possible fill staging 300 ft away.
constraint: There is no approved deep-basin design. Calculate the water load and compare smaller basins or approved containers.
reason: Reject: requested depth exceeds berm, undersized liner, enormous water load and insufficient bags.
extra: Approved tanks/containers, water delivery, smaller shallow basin with approval

title: Clinic Sanitation Collection
situation: A temporary clinic needs an adult-managed non-potable water reserve.
mission: Assess a small adult-managed non-potable water reserve for a temporary clinic.
site: Suggested inside footprint 10 × 10 ft and depth 0.25 ft; fill staging 300 ft away via a dry level pedestrian route.
constraint: No vehicle fits the last 300 ft. Water is not for drinking or handwashing; compare collection with delivered containers.
reason: Conditional: movement is likely limiting; delivered approved containers may be easier.
extra: Liner, signage, barrier, overflow and authorized sanitation-use plan

title: Shelter Tarp Floor
situation: A dry shelter staging area needs a plastic ground cover held against light wind.
mission: Hold a ground-cover tarp in place for a dry shelter staging area.
site: Ground-cover footprint 20 × 12 ft; potential fill staging 60 ft away.
constraint: This is ground cover, not an overhead shelter. Keep edges out of accessible walking routes.
reason: Reasonable in light wind on dry ground; do not infer structural anchoring strength.
extra: Tarp, edge markings and trip-hazard control

title: Temporary Privacy Partitions
situation: A shelter needs privacy screens on an approved indoor frame system.
mission: Plan supplementary ballast for approved shelter privacy-screen frames.
site: Six approved base stations; supervisor requests two bags per station. Possible fill staging 80 ft from the entrance.
constraint: Only the rated frame system may be used; keep exits open and protect the floor.
reason: Reasonable only with the supplied rated system and supervisor-approved ballast.
extra: Rated frames, floor protection, accessible egress and supervisor check

title: Mobile Charging Tent
situation: A shelter requests supplementary ballast for an approved charging tent.
mission: Plan supplementary ballast for an approved mobile charging tent.
site: Eight approved ballast stations; site supervisor requests four bags per station. Potential fill staging 150 ft away.
constraint: The manufacturer still controls anchoring. Sandbag quantities do not establish a wind rating; plan indoor shelter for thunderstorms.
reason: Conditional supplement only. Suspend use and shelter indoors for threatening weather.
extra: Rated anchors, cable covers, electrical supervision and weather shutdown

title: Emergency Wayfinding Signs
situation: Temporary signs are needed at an emergency assistance site.
mission: Place temporary wayfinding signs throughout an emergency assistance site.
site: Ten approved stands; supervisor requests two bags per stand. Signs extend along a 600 ft pedestrian route; possible fill staging at the midpoint.
constraint: The route stays accessible. Allow time for distributed placement and checking visibility.
reason: Reasonable with approved stands; distributed placement and visibility may dominate.
extra: Reflective signage, rated stands, lights if work continues

title: Debris-Sorting Tarp
situation: Public works is sorting clean storm debris on a closed paved area.
mission: Hold down a debris-sorting ground tarp before Public Works begins sorting.
site: Ground tarp footprint 40 × 20 ft; possible fill staging 200 ft away.
constraint: Adult crews inspect debris and the site. Tarp ballast is not hazardous-material containment.
reason: Reasonable for temporary ground-cover edging; sorting and debris disposal remain separate.
extra: Tarp, exclusion, labeled sorting zones and removal plan

title: Potentially Contaminated Runoff
situation: Responders report runoff from an unknown spill approaching a storm inlet.
mission: Assess temporary protection of a storm inlet from potentially contaminated runoff.
site: 50 ft threatened boundary; potential clean-zone fill staging 100 ft away.
constraint: Planning only: hazardous-material responders authorize all work, containment destinations and PPE. Students never handle contamination.
reason: Conditional on hazardous-material responder direction; source control and drain protection may be better.
extra: Responder-specified PPE, compatible liner, exclusion, collection/disposal

title: Flooded Maintenance Yard
situation: Water from a maintenance yard may contain oil and other contaminants.
mission: Assess clean-side protection around a flooded maintenance yard.
site: 80 ft affected boundary; possible clean staging 250 ft away.
constraint: Water may contain oil or other contaminants. Trained responders control entry, compatible materials, recovery and disposal.
reason: Requested bags and fill exceed supply; prioritize isolation, professional recovery and a shorter approved segment.
extra: Hazmat coordination, compatible liner, lights, disposal and exclusion

title: Sand Delivery on a Closed Hill
situation: A school on a steep street needs diversion, but the sand truck cannot climb the closed route.
mission: Keep hillside school runoff away from occupied areas despite difficult delivery access.
site: 90 ft affected frontage; nearest approved sand drop is 600 ft away. The final pedestrian route is dry but uphill.
constraint: The delivery truck cannot reach the school. The earliest sand drop is 1 hour after assignment; propose a safe last-mile plan.
reason: Useful if last-mile transfer can finish; choose a closer approved fill site or mechanized transfer.
extra: Delivery plan, sheet, route control, rest and additional transfer capacity

title: Overnight Supply Depot
situation: A dry supply depot has time to protect one exposed side before a forecast shallow rise.
mission: Protect the exposed side of a supply depot before the forecast shallow rise.
site: 120 ft frontage; forecast water depth 6 in; possible fill staging 240 ft away.
constraint: This may require overnight work. Fill must be delivered; include lights, meals, rotation and verified power.
reason: Conditional; rotation, food, lighting and delivery staging are as important as bags.
extra: Sheets, powered lights, meals, warm breaks, staged fill and relief workers

title: Two Sites, One Workforce
situation: A shelter entrance and an empty recreation building both request protection.
mission: Prioritize and plan protection at two sites sharing the same response resources.
site: Shelter: 30 ft affected entrance approach. Empty recreation building: 60 ft frontage, forecast water depth 6 in. Potential fill staging is 100 ft from shelter and 400 ft from recreation building.
constraint: Shelter request is due in 1 hour; recreation request in 3 hours. Protect people and essential access before empty property.
reason: Combined plan exceeds bag/fill stock; prioritize shelter, reduce or abandon second request.
extra: Priority communication, separate deadlines, accessible shelter entrance and phased allocation
